note.question: When should a firm assemble equally capable or productively diverse teams, and how should it tilt performance pay to preserve cooperation without enabling team members to collude?
note.overview: A principal contracts with two mutually monitoring agents in an infinitely repeated hidden-effort game. The desired joint-work path must be a Pareto-undominated subgame-perfect equilibrium, and the contract must simultaneously sustain cooperation and prevent the agents from coordinating on a preferred collusive equilibrium.

components.label: Pareto-undominated subgame-perfect joint-work equilibrium with collusion-proof contracting
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Pareto-undominated subgame-perfect joint-work equilibrium with collusion-proof contracting. Cooperation 1 and 2 combine no-current-deviation constraints with self-enforcing stage-game punishments. Proposition 1 characterizes how productive heterogeneity changes cooperative wages. Lemma 2 and Proposition 2 characterize stationary correlated collusion and show that it never arises in cross-functional teams but binds for sufficiently patient agents in functional teams; the optimal contract then blocks collusion through the more productive agent.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At the beginning of the infinite relationship, the principal commits to stationary wages paid after success or failure. In each period both agents simultaneously choose work or shirk, privately from the principal but observable to each other. Success or failure is realized and wages are paid. After a deviation the agents can use a stage-game Nash equilibrium as a grim-trigger punishment; before play they may also coordinate on a stationary correlated subgame-perfect equilibrium that Pareto-dominates the principal's intended path.
